author: lperlind
body:
This patch adds a private arena for the font where the font itself is located and where tables can allocate whatever they want from. This removes all cases of needing a 'destroy' proc so I have removed it for now.

The arena uses some heuristics to guess what size it should allocate but it can be overriden by the user.

Additionally the arena's are auto cleaned up if a table fails to load. This is done with the 
`read_arena_context_cleanup_begin` procedure which takes a reader context and at the end of scope will 
reset the arena to where it started when the procedure was called given that `ctx.ok` is false.

body:
# Pull Request Checklist

### Note to first-time contributors: Please open a discussion post in [Discussions](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/discussions) and describe your changes before submitting a pull request.

**Before submitting, make sure you've checked the following:**

- [x] **Target branch:** Please verify that the pull request targets the `dev` branch.
- [x] **Description:** Provide a concise description of the changes made in this pull request.
- [x] **Changelog:** Ensure a changelog entry following the format of [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/) is added at the bottom of the PR description.
- [x] **Documentation:** Have you updated relevant documentation [Open WebUI Docs](https://github.com/open-webui/docs), or other documentation sources?
- [x] **Dependencies:** Are there any new dependencies? Have you updated the dependency versions in the documentation?
- [x] **Testing:** Have you written and run sufficient tests to validate the changes?
- [x] **Code review:** Have you performed a self-review of your code, addressing any coding standard issues and ensuring adherence to the project's coding standards?
- [x] **Prefix:** To clearly categorize this pull request, prefix the pull request title using one of the following:
  - **BREAKING CHANGE**: Significant changes that may affect compatibility
  - **build**: Changes that affect the build system or external dependencies
  - **ci**: Changes to our continuous integration processes or workflows
  - **chore**: Refactor, cleanup, or other non-functional code changes
  - **docs**: Documentation update or addition
  - **feat**: Introduces a new feature or enhancement to the codebase
  - **fix**: Bug fix or error correction
  - **i18n**: Internationalization or localization changes
  - **perf**: Performance improvement
  - **refactor**: Code restructuring for better maintainability, readability, or scalability
  - **style**: Changes that do not affect the meaning of the code (white space, formatting, missing semi-colons, etc.)
  - **test**: Adding missing tests or correcting existing tests
  - **WIP**: Work in progress, a temporary label for incomplete or ongoing work

# Changelog Entry

### Description

All web search results per search query were assigned the same source id before, despite containing content from different URLs. Thus, URLs wouldn't be cited correctly.

This PR fixes the source id assignment for the case of bypassed embedding&retrieval, making sure every URL gets its own source id.

### Fixed

- Return one result file per URL in chat_web_search_handler

### Screenshot

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/71b4e94e-e227-4891-a8c3-2d51f6861c66)

---

### Additional Information

This fixes https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/discussions/11205 for web search (together with https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/12507). I think further fixes are needed for RAG with knowledge bases and potentially also tool results (https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/discussions/10595). The case of regular file uploads within the chat is fine.

It works in conjunction with additional sources, e.g. from file uploads, or multiple search queries.

### Alternatives considered

https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/discussions/11205#discussioncomment-12684414 , but I think that would assign a different source id to every chunk in embed&retrieval mode.

author: pavel-farkas
body:
port of KECA-44 for 5.4

Kazoo uses Freeswitch recording functionality to record various types of data: voicemails, calls, prompts, announcements, etc. All these recording actions generate events informing about recording progress: start, stop, pause, etc. These events themselves do not carry information about what was the origin and purpose of the recording. Before introduction of API for call recording_status ([KZOO-531](https://oomacorp.atlassian.net/browse/KZOO-531)), there was no need to track the origin of recording - ecallmagr monitored only RECORD_STOP events and then decides if and where to store resulting recorded file.

API for call recording_status feature required listeners for all recording events and based on these events it updates recording status. Therefore, now there is a need to filter out recording events not related to call recording - events produced by VM, prompts, etc recording.

Kazoo crash described in the parent ticket ([SUPP-681](https://oomacorp.atlassian.net/browse/SUPP-681)) is caused by handling of VM events as call recording events - event handler/listener tries to read information which VM event object does not contain.

This PR aims to fix that.

following the guidelines for hotfix, the code changes are minimal and possible without any side effects leading to regression
logic here is very simple, these commits make sure that only call recording event objects will have Recording.Name key with value always set (never undefined)
in other recording events (VM, prompts, etc) Recording.Name key will be missing, which makes it a parameter to base filter on

author: ramppdev
body:
Closes #29 by adding a `transfer` argument to all models. This allows for handling the transfer argument as follows:
- `autrainer fetch` and `autrainer train`: remove `transfer` if a model checkpoint is provided -> no weights need to be downloaded
- `autrainer inference`: override `transfer` to `None` as we will always load a checkpoint

### Up for debate
- Testability to verify this functionality is very limited, not sure how to or even if to test this; of course i checked everything manually but i dont have a good automated solution to do so right now
- The state of `transfer` is removed from the final `model.yaml` and will be set to `null` if a `model_checkpoint` is provided; the original config is still present in the `.hydra/config.yaml` and the original model config so full reproducibility is still given


### Additional changes
- This adds the `transfer` functionality to all our models, allowing to load all of them with pretrained weights. The only exceptions are `AudioRNNModel`, `FFNN`, and `SeqFFNN`. These will raise an error when you pass a truthy value for `transfer`. The reason they also have this argument now it to have a uniform interface for `AbstractModel`.

- Since we now have the ability to load all models with `transfer=None`, most tests will do so, mostly resolving the issue that tests may fail due to downloading model states here: https://github.com/autrainer/autrainer/pull/46#issuecomment-2752115788
For `TorchvisionModel`, we still keep the transfer test as `efficientnet_b0` is a small model state and verifies that overriding the last layer works.

### Breaking changes
Whisper, TDNN, and W2V2 models can now be initialized with random weights, so all of their pretrained-configs (ending with `-T`) were either newly created or include `transfer: true` now.

body:
### Update [requests](https://pypi.org/project/requests) from **2.28.2** to **2.32.3**.


<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 2.32.3
   ```
   -------------------

**Bugfixes**
- Fixed bug breaking the ability to specify custom SSLContexts in sub-classes of
  HTTPAdapter. (6716)
- Fixed issue where Requests started failing to run on Python versions compiled
  without the `ssl` module. (6724)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.32.2
   ```
   -------------------

**Deprecations**
- To provide a more stable migration for custom HTTPAdapters impacted
  by the CVE changes in 2.32.0, we've renamed `_get_connection` to
  a new public API, `get_connection_with_tls_context`. Existing custom
  HTTPAdapters will need to migrate their code to use this new API.
  `get_connection` is considered deprecated in all versions of Requests>=2.32.0.

  A minimal (2-line) example has been provided in the linked PR to ease
  migration, but we strongly urge users to evaluate if their custom adapter
  is subject to the same issue described in CVE-2024-35195. (6710)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.32.1
   ```
   -------------------

**Bugfixes**
- Add missing test certs to the sdist distributed on PyPI.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.32.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Security**
- Fixed an issue where setting `verify=False` on the first request from a
  Session will cause subsequent requests to the _same origin_ to also ignore
  cert verification, regardless of the value of `verify`.
  (https://github.com/psf/requests/security/advisories/GHSA-9wx4-h78v-vm56)

**Improvements**
- `verify=True` now reuses a global SSLContext which should improve
  request time variance between first and subsequent requests. It should
  also minimize certificate load time on Windows systems when using a Python
  version built with OpenSSL 3.x. (6667)
- Requests now supports optional use of character detection
  (`chardet` or `charset_normalizer`) when repackaged or vendored.
  This enables `pip` and other projects to minimize their vendoring
  surface area. The `Response.text()` and `apparent_encoding` APIs
  will default to `utf-8` if neither library is present. (6702)

**Bugfixes**
- Fixed bug in length detection where emoji length was incorrectly
  calculated in the request content-length. (6589)
- Fixed deserialization bug in JSONDecodeError. (6629)
- Fixed bug where an extra leading `/` (path separator) could lead
  urllib3 to unnecessarily reparse the request URI. (6644)

**Deprecations**

- Requests has officially added support for CPython 3.12 (6503)
- Requests has officially added support for PyPy 3.9 and 3.10 (6641)
- Requests has officially dropped support for CPython 3.7 (6642)
- Requests has officially dropped support for PyPy 3.7 and 3.8 (6641)

**Documentation**
- Various typo fixes and doc improvements.

**Packaging**
- Requests has started adopting some modern packaging practices.
  The source files for the projects (formerly `requests`) is now located
  in `src/requests` in the Requests sdist. (6506)
- Starting in Requests 2.33.0, Requests will migrate to a PEP 517 build system
  using `hatchling`. This should not impact the average user, but extremely old
  versions of packaging utilities may have issues with the new packaging format.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.31.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Security**
- Versions of Requests between v2.3.0 and v2.30.0 are vulnerable to potential
  forwarding of `Proxy-Authorization` headers to destination servers when
  following HTTPS redirects.

  When proxies are defined with user info (`https://user:passproxy:8080`), Requests
  will construct a `Proxy-Authorization` header that is attached to the request to
  authenticate with the proxy.

  In cases where Requests receives a redirect response, it previously reattached
  the `Proxy-Authorization` header incorrectly, resulting in the value being
  sent through the tunneled connection to the destination server. Users who rely on
  defining their proxy credentials in the URL are *strongly* encouraged to upgrade
  to Requests 2.31.0+ to prevent unintentional leakage and rotate their proxy
  credentials once the change has been fully deployed.

  Users who do not use a proxy or do not supply their proxy credentials through
  the user information portion of their proxy URL are not subject to this
  vulnerability.

  Full details can be read in our [Github Security Advisory](https://github.com/psf/requests/security/advisories/GHSA-j8r2-6x86-q33q)
  and [CVE-2023-32681](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-32681).
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.30.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Dependencies**
- ⚠️ Added support for urllib3 2.0. ⚠️

  This may contain minor breaking changes so we advise careful testing and
  reviewing https://urllib3.readthedocs.io/en/latest/v2-migration-guide.html
  prior to upgrading.

  Users who wish to stay on urllib3 1.x can pin to `urllib3<2`.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.29.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Improvements**

- Requests now defers chunked requests to the urllib3 implementation to improve
  standardization. (6226)
- Requests relaxes header component requirements to support bytes/str subclasses. (6356)
   ```
   
  
</details>

  - PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/requests
  - Changelog: https://data.safetycli.com/changelogs/requests/
  - Docs: https://requests.readthedocs.io
</details>

python
from environs import env


Changes:

- `default` values are expected to be their in their deserialized form.
  _Backwards-incompatible_: Passing serialized values to `default`
  is no longer supported.

python
from datetime import date, timedelta
import environs

 DO
enable_login = env.bool("ENABLE_LOGIN", True)
ttl = env.timedelta("TTL", default=timedelta(seconds=600))
release_date = env.date("RELEASE", date(2025, 1, 7))
numbers = env.list("FOO", [1.0, 2.0, 3.0], subcast=float)

 DON'T
enable_login = env.bool("ENABLE_LOGIN", "true")
ttl = env.timedelta("TTL", default=600)
release_date = env.date("RELEASE", "2025-01-07")
numbers = env.list("NUMBERS", "1,2,42", subcast=float)


The exceptions to this rule are the Django-related functions, which
accept string defaults.

python

**Before submitting, make sure you've checked the following:**

- [x] **Target branch:** Please verify that the pull request targets the `dev` branch.
- [x] **Description:** Provide a concise description of the changes made in this pull request.
- [x] **Changelog:** Ensure a changelog entry following the format of [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/) is added at the bottom of the PR description.
- [x] **Documentation:** Have you updated relevant documentation [Open WebUI Docs](https://github.com/open-webui/docs), or other documentation sources?
- [x] **Dependencies:** Are there any new dependencies? Have you updated the dependency versions in the documentation?
- [x] **Testing:** Have you written and run sufficient tests to validate the changes?
- [x] **Code review:** Have you performed a self-review of your code, addressing any coding standard issues and ensuring adherence to the project's coding standards?
- [x] **Prefix:** To clearly categorize this pull request, prefix the pull request title using one of the following:
  - **BREAKING CHANGE**: Significant changes that may affect compatibility
  - **build**: Changes that affect the build system or external dependencies
  - **ci**: Changes to our continuous integration processes or workflows
  - **chore**: Refactor, cleanup, or other non-functional code changes
  - **docs**: Documentation update or addition
  - **feat**: Introduces a new feature or enhancement to the codebase
  - **fix**: Bug fix or error correction
  - **i18n**: Internationalization or localization changes
  - **perf**: Performance improvement
  - **refactor**: Code restructuring for better maintainability, readability, or scalability
  - **style**: Changes that do not affect the meaning of the code (white space, formatting, missing semi-colons, etc.)
  - **test**: Adding missing tests or correcting existing tests
  - **WIP**: Work in progress, a temporary label for incomplete or ongoing work

# Changelog Entry

### Description

All web search results per search query were assigned the same source id before, despite containing content from different URLs. Thus, URLs wouldn't be cited correctly.

This PR fixes the source id assignment for the case of web search with embedding&retrieval, making sure every URL gets its own collection and thus source id.

### Fixed

- Return one result file and collection per URL in chat_web_search_handler

---

### Additional Information

This fixes https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/discussions/11205 for web search (together with https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/12506). I think further fixes are needed for RAG with knowledge bases and potentially also tool results (https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/discussions/10595). The case of regular file uploads within the chat is fine.

It works in conjunction with additional sources, e.g. from file uploads, or multiple search queries.

### Alternatives considered

https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/discussions/11205#discussioncomment-12684414 , but I think that would assign a different source id to every chunk in embed&retrieval mode.

body:
## Description
This PR addresses issue #211 where Windsurf clients are unable to parse the input schema for the `jira_create_issue` tool. The issue occurs because Windsurf has trouble parsing array-type parameters in the tool's input schema.

## Changes
- Changed the `components` parameter in the `jira_create_issue` tool from an array type to a string type
- Updated the parameter description to specify it accepts a comma-separated list
- Added preprocessing logic in `server.py` to convert the comma-separated string to a list before passing to the JiraFetcher
- Updated the unit test to use the new string format while maintaining the same assertion

## Why This Approach
This approach maintains the existing behavior for all clients while making the tool compatible with Windsurf. The string-to-list conversion happens at the API boundary in `server.py`, keeping the JiraFetcher implementation clean with its well-defined `list[str] | None` contract.

## Fixes
Closes #211

If you still encounter a runtime error after applying these changes:

1.  **Check Console:** Open your browser's developer console (usually F12). Look for the *exact* error message. It will often point to the specific line or component causing the issue.
2.  **Verify Installation:** Ensure `react-icons` is correctly installed: `npm install react-icons` or `yarn add react-icons`.

author: kennedyrichard
body:
Block comments allow people to uncomment/comment a whole code block by adding/removing a single '/' character.

None of the existing examples clearly demonstrates this ability, so I thought it'd be useful to do so here.

The chapter is already very small, so adding a few extra lines should be acceptable.

I actually learned this from [Haskell](https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Haskell/Variables_and_functions#Comments), although I don't use it as often as Rust.

Toggling an entire code block by adding/removing a single character seems very, very useful, so I think it is worth teaching it to users and it deserves a prominent spot in this popular learning resource.

body:
The deployment is currently failing due to a missing package required to install the `openssl` gem. Specifically, the `libssl-dev` package is no longer included in the latest patch versions of the official `Ruby` Docker images (3.4.2, 3.3.7, 3.2.8), see [this commit](https://github.com/docker-library/ruby/commit/193c69e863a4c2bf86f6e323cb294fe1b8e1e845#diff-8d7a21b017921bb88eaf71656b7b5767203db16e8126fc1e5ad2a9ba0bc542f5L237).

We didn't encounter this issue previously because our deployments used an earlier `Ruby` image that still included `libssl-dev` by default. Now that we've upgraded to `Ruby 3.4.2`, we need to install `libssl-dev`.

We probably need to install this package in the rest of the apps that uses `webauthn`.

author: ai-kanban-test-env[bot]
body:
This PR addresses ticket #01960ba4-81a0-7000-b3a0-85e676dc7c53:

Migrate all components from forwardRef to ref as a Prop
----------
Refined Ticket: Migrate All Components from `forwardRef` to Passing `ref` as a Prop

---

### Context & Goal
React 19 introduces improved ref forwarding capabilities, allowing components to accept `ref` as a regular prop rather than relying on `forwardRef`. This migration aims to simplify component definitions, improve type safety, and align with React 19 best practices.

---

### Assumptions
- The project is using React 19 or later, which supports passing `ref` as a prop.
- All components currently using `forwardRef` should be updated.
- Consumers of these components will be updated separately if needed.
- No change in component behavior is expected; this is a refactoring task.

---

### Potential Solution Approaches Considered
1. **Update all components to accept `ref` as a prop, remove `forwardRef`** (Chosen)
2. Wrap existing components with an adapter that converts prop `ref` to forwarded ref (adds complexity)
3. Use a codemod to automate migration (out of scope for this manual refinement)
4. Keep `forwardRef` but add support for `ref` as a prop (unnecessary duplication)
5. Migrate only some components selectively (inconsistent, not aligned with ticket)
6. Rewrite components as class components (unnecessary and counterproductive)
7. Remove ref support entirely (breaks functionality)

**Chosen Approach:**  
Update all components that currently use `forwardRef` to accept `ref` as a normal prop, removing the `forwardRef` wrapper. This is straightforward, aligns with React 19, and reduces complexity.

---

### Action Plan

#### 1. Identify all components using `forwardRef`
- Search for `forwardRef` usage in the codebase, primarily under `src/frontend/components/ui/` and `src/frontend/components/`.
- Confirm which components are wrapped with `forwardRef`.

#### 2. For each identified component:
- Remove the `forwardRef` wrapper.
- Change the component to a standard function component.
- Add `ref` as an explicit prop, typed appropriately (e.g., `ref?: React.Ref<HTMLButtonElement>`).
- Pass the `ref` prop to the relevant DOM element inside the component.
- Update prop types/interfaces accordingly.
- Ensure no other logic depends on `forwardRef` behavior.

#### 3. Update component exports
- Ensure components are exported as standard function components.

#### 4. Verify imports and usage
- Check if any internal usage relies on the old `forwardRef` signature.
- If so, update those usages to pass `ref` as a prop.

#### 5. Testing
- Run existing tests to ensure no regressions.
- Manually verify that refs are correctly attached in the UI.

---

### Components Likely Affected (based on typical usage patterns)
- `src/frontend/components/ui/button.tsx`
- `src/frontend/components/ui/input.tsx`
- `src/frontend/components/ui/textarea.tsx`
- `src/frontend/components/ui/select.tsx`
- `src/frontend/components/ui/checkbox.tsx`
- `src/frontend/components/ui/switch.tsx`
- `src/frontend/components/ui/toggle.tsx`
- `src/frontend/components/ui/toggle-group.tsx`
- `src/frontend/components/ui/accordion.tsx`
- `src/frontend/components/ui/dialog.tsx`
- `src/frontend/components/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx`
- `src/frontend/components/ui/hover-card.tsx`
- `src/frontend/components/ui/popover.tsx`
- `src/frontend/components/ui/tooltip.tsx`
- `src/frontend/components/ui/menubar.tsx`
- `src/frontend/components/ui/navigation-menu.tsx`
- `src/frontend/components/ui/alert-dialog.tsx`
- `src/frontend/components/ui/drawer.tsx`
- `src/frontend/components/ui/sheet.tsx`
- `src/frontend/components/ui/context-menu.tsx`
- (Confirm exact list during implementation)

---

### File & Directory Changes

**Update (remove `forwardRef`, add `ref` prop):**
- `src/frontend/components/ui/*.tsx` (all components using `forwardRef`)
- Potentially `src/frontend/components/index.tsx` if it re-exports affected components

**No new files or deletions expected.**

---

### Deliverables
- All relevant components migrated to accept `ref` as a prop.
- No usage of `forwardRef` remains in the codebase.
- Prop types updated accordingly.
- Tests pass without regression.

---

### Notes
- This migration is purely internal refactoring; no API changes expected for consumers who pass `ref` as a prop.
- If any consumer code breaks, coordinate with relevant teams for follow-up tickets.
- Document the new pattern in the project’s component development guidelines.
----------
Testing strategy:

1. **Static Analysis: Verify Migration Completeness**
   - Perform a recursive search to ensure **no usage of `forwardRef` remains** in the codebase:
     - `grep -r "forwardRef" src/frontend/components/`
     - The result should be empty, confirming all wrappers have been removed.
   - Optionally, extend the search to the entire `src/` directory to catch any missed instances.
   - Search for `React.forwardRef` as well, in case of fully qualified usage:
     - `grep -r "React\.forwardRef" src/frontend/components/`
   - Confirm that all affected components explicitly declare a `ref` prop in their type definitions:
     - Search for `ref:` or `ref?` in component prop interfaces or destructured props.

2. **Unit & Integration Testing: Verify Ref Functionality**
   - For each migrated component:
     - **Write or update unit tests** that:
       - Render the component with a `ref` prop (using `React.createRef()` or `useRef()`).
       - Assert that the `ref.current` points to the expected DOM element after mount.
       - Example: For `<Button ref={ref} />`, check `expect(ref.current).toBeInstanceOf(HTMLButtonElement)`.
     - If existing tests already cover ref attachment, review them to ensure they pass without modification.
   - For composite components (e.g., `Dialog`, `Popover`), verify that refs are forwarded correctly to the intended DOM nodes.

3. **Manual UI Testing: Regression & Ref Attachment**
   - In a running development environment:
     - Use React DevTools to inspect components and confirm that refs passed as props are attached to the correct DOM elements.
     - Interact with UI elements (buttons, inputs, dialogs, etc.) to ensure no runtime errors or warnings related to refs.
     - Test focus management, keyboard navigation, and any features relying on refs (e.g., auto-focus, scroll-to-element).
   - Pay special attention to complex components like dropdowns, modals, and tooltips, where ref forwarding is often critical.

4. **Consumer Usage Verification**
   - Search for internal usages of affected components within the codebase:
     - `grep -r "<ComponentName" src/frontend/`
     - Confirm that refs are now passed as props, not via `ref` on a `forwardRef`-wrapped component.
   - If any internal consumers relied on the old `forwardRef` signature (e.g., using `ref` on the component instance), ensure they are updated accordingly.

5. **Regression Testing**
   - Run the full automated test suite (unit, integration, e2e if available) to detect any unintended side effects.
   - Pay attention to snapshot tests that might capture component structure changes due to the removal of `forwardRef`.

6. **Type Safety Validation**
   - Run the TypeScript compiler (`tsc --noEmit`) to ensure all components and their consumers type-check correctly with the new `ref` prop signatures.
   - Confirm no new type errors related to refs.

7. **Documentation & Code Review**

author: priyad17
body:
## Description

This PR introduces the following changes to the `StockOutTable.js` component:

### Session-Based Authentication:
- Replaced `localStorage` with `sessionStorage` for managing authentication.
- Authentication data now persists **only for the current browser session** and is cleared automatically when the browser is closed.

### Login and Logout Enhancements:
- Added a `handleLogin` function to store authentication data in `sessionStorage` with a **30-day expiry**.
- Added a `handleLogout` function to clear authentication data and reset the login state.

### 👥 Improved User Role Management:
- Dynamically sets **user roles, email, and country code** based on the login response (currently mocked).

### 🛠️ Code Refactoring:
- Updated the `checkExistingAuth` function to validate and clear expired or invalid authentication data from `sessionStorage`.

---

## Changes Made
- Replaced all instances of `localStorage` with `sessionStorage`.
- Added `handleLogin` and `handleLogout` functions for managing authentication state.
- Updated `checkExistingAuth` for session-based authentication.
- Modified `LoginModal` to trigger `handleLogin` upon successful login.
- Added a **logout button** in the `TopBar` component to allow users to log out manually.
## 🧪 Testing Instructions

### 🔓 Login Flow:
1. Start the application.
2. Confirm the **login modal appears** if no valid session exists.
3. Log in and verify that the **dashboard** is displayed.

### ♻️ Session Persistence:
1. Refresh the page — the user should remain logged in during the **same browser session**.
2. Close and reopen the browser — the **login modal** should appear again.

### 🚪 Logout Flow:
1. Click the **logout button** in the `TopBar`.
2. Confirm the **login modal** appears and the session is cleared.

Resolves: #4

author: benbriel
body:
This update introduces significant refactoring across the codebase, including the transition to YAML for configuration, improved GUI components, enhanced logging and a new Sequence object. The version is updated to 0.5.0-alpha.

# Changes
- Removed Scripts (refactored into `laser_setup.cli`)
- Replaced `.ini` files with YAML config management, powered by OmegaConf and Hydra
- Added new way of setting up adapters, matching "*IDN?" response
- Added easy way of initializing the configuration wth `laser_setup init`
- Centralized all PyQt imports and added qtpy for flexibility with Qt libraries
- Added new Widgets to the MainWindow
- Added Sequences, a way of running multiple Procedures of different types (still in development, but functional)
- Added a few patches to the PyMeasure library
- Added `uv.lock`
- Changed Python version requirements (add `3.13`, drop `3.9`)

This PR adds the ability for users to import an existing wallet using their 12 or 24-word recovery phrase, with an intuitive user interface and enhanced usability features.#83

- Improved UX with visual guidance and tooltips for users

- Dynamic adjustment based on selected word count (12 or 24)

author: osekitaemmanuel
body:
## Overview

This PR implements a blockchain-based textile authentication system using Clarity smart contracts. The system enables verification of textile producers, certification of materials, documentation of testing, and tracking through the supply chain.

## Changes

- Added four smart contracts:
  - `producer-verification.clar`: Validates legitimate textile manufacturers
  - `material-certification.clar`: Records fiber content and production methods
  - `testing-verification.clar`: Documents compliance with quality standards
  - `supply-chain.clar`: Tracks textiles from raw materials to finished products
- Added comprehensive README with setup and usage instructions
- Added test suite using Vitest

## Testing

All contracts have been tested using Vitest. Tests verify:
- Producer registration and verification
- Material certification
- Test result recording
- Supply chain tracking and ownership transfer

## Deployment

These contracts can be deployed to the Stacks blockchain using Clarinet.

## Future Work

- Add UI for interacting with the contracts
- Implement more sophisticated querying capabilities
- Add integration with physical verification methods (QR codes, NFC tags)

author: wonderwhy-er
body:
# Add URL Support to read_file Command and Improve Code Structure

This PR adds the ability to fetch files from URLs using the `read_file` command. It also significantly refactors the codebase to improve maintainability through a more modular structure and adds important timeout handling for search operations.

## Changes

### URL Support
- Added `isUrl` parameter to `ReadFileArgsSchema` to support URL fetching
- Split `readFile` into dedicated `readFileFromUrl` and `readFileFromDisk` functions
- Implemented cross-fetch for HTTP requests with timeout handling
- Updated tool descriptions to indicate URL support

### Code Structure Improvements
- Refactored server.ts by moving command handlers to separate modules:
  - `command-handlers.ts` for command management
  - `edit-search-handlers.ts` for text operations
  - `filesystem-handlers.ts` for file operations
  - `terminal-handlers.ts` for terminal commands
  - `process-handlers.ts` for process management
- Streamlined error handling to upper layer
- Simplified analytics capture patterns

### Performance & Reliability
- Added `withTimeout` utility function for controlled timeouts
- Implemented 30-second default timeouts for search operations
- Made timeouts customizable via `timeoutMs` parameter
- Improved error messages for timed-out operations

The `read_file` command can now seamlessly handle both local files and remote content using the same interface.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c92c2b28-f727-45c6-b2d8-e3bc4ff29f07)

## Potential follow-ups (out of scope for this PR)
- Add "return format" parameter to allow returning full HTML pages, plain text, or markdown
- Allow query of common structured formats (HTML, JSON, CSV) to retrieve structure or parts


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
  - Added URL support for file editing, allowing retrieval and display of web-based text and images with built-in timeout protection.
  - Introduced default timeouts for search operations to improve responsiveness and notify users of lengthy processes.

- **Documentation**
  - Updated user guides to reflect the new URL retrieval capability and enhanced timeout settings.

- **Refactor**
  - Consolidated and modularized command handling and filesystem operations to enhance reliability and maintainability.

This PR adds GitHub Actions workflows for:

- Testing (test.yml): Runs on every push/PR, includes unit/integration tests and linting.

- Model Evaluation (evaluate.yml): Runs after tests, evaluates model performance, fails if below threshold, and uploads metrics.
 
- Docker Build (build.yml): Builds and pushes Docker image to DockerHub on push to main.

Also includes updates in src/ to support automation.

body:
Dev fin

Okay, let's refactor `RepoTxtFetcher` into a mothership component and several subcomponents within the `/components/repo/` directory.

We'll create:

1.  `RepoTxtFetcher.tsx` (Mothership)
2.  `/components/repo/SettingsModal.tsx` (For URL, Token inputs, and Fetch button)
3.  `/components/repo/FileList.tsx` (For displaying and selecting files)
4.  `/components/repo/SelectedFilesPreview.tsx` (For previewing selected file content)
5.  `/components/repo/RequestInput.tsx` (For the Kwork textarea and copy button)
6.  `/components/repo/ProgressBar.tsx` (For the mocked progress bar)

Here's the refactored code:

**1. Mothership Component (`RepoTxtFetcher.tsx`)**

**2. Settings Modal (`/components/repo/SettingsModal.tsx`)**

**3. File List (`/components/repo/FileList.tsx`)**

**4. Selected Files Preview (`/components/repo/SelectedFilesPreview.tsx`)**

**5. Request Input (`/components/repo/RequestInput.tsx`)**

**6. Progress Bar (`/components/repo/ProgressBar.tsx`)**

**Key Changes and Considerations:**

1.  **Component Structure:** The logic and UI are now split into logical units.
2.  **Settings Modal:** The URL/Token inputs are in a collapsible section triggered by a `FaCircleChevronDown` icon. `AnimatePresence` provides smooth opening/closing.
3.  **State Management:** Most state remains in the `RepoTxtFetcher` (mothership) as it's needed across multiple children or for core logic. Props and callbacks are used for communication.
4.  **Helper Functions:** `getLanguage`, `getDisplayName`, and `groupFilesByFolder` are defined where they are used or passed down. You could create a central `utils/repoUtils.ts` file for them if preferred.
5.  **Intro Text:** Updated to follow the step-by-step format with emojis and consistent language.
6.  **Preview Section Position:** `SelectedFilesPreview` is now rendered *before* `FileList`.
7.  **Mocked Progress Bar:**
    *   A dedicated `ProgressBar` component handles the visual display based on `status` and `progress`.
    *   The simulation logic (`startProgressSimulation`, `stopProgressSimulation`) using `setInterval` and `setTimeout` resides in the `RepoTxtFetcher` where the fetch is initiated.
    *   It simulates a 13-second duration, updating progress frequently.
    *   It caps at 69% if the actual fetch takes longer than 13 seconds.
    *   It correctly sets progress to 100% on success or 0% on error, clearing the simulation timers.
    *   Cleanup using `useEffect` return function and `useCallback` for stable timer functions.
    *   The progress bar and status text are now shown conditionally, mainly during the initial load or if an error occurs.
8.  **Prop Drilling:** There's some prop drilling (e.g., `selectedFiles`, `files`), which is acceptable for this level of nesting. If the component grew much larger, context might become more beneficial.
9.  **Dependencies:** `useCallback` is used for handler functions passed down as props or used in `useEffect` to prevent unnecessary re-renders or effect executions. Dependency arrays are carefully managed.
10. **Styling:** Tailwind classes are maintained. Minor adjustments were made for layout and consistency (e.g., added `custom-scrollbar` class placeholder - you might need to define this globally if you want custom scrollbars). Added some subtle hover effects and transitions.
11. **Accessibility:** Added `aria-labelledby` to the checkbox input in `FileList` for better screen reader support (though simple `label` wrapping might be preferred if structure allowed). Added `title` attributes for tooltips.
12. **Ref Forwarding:** The `kworkInputRef` is correctly passed down from `RepoTxtFetcher` to `RequestInput` and attached to the `textarea`.

Remember to install any necessary dependencies (`framer-motion`, `react-icons`, `react-syntax-highlighter`). Place the new files in the correct `/components/repo/` subfolder and update imports accordingly.

Okay, I understand. Let's move the "Fetch Files" button back out of the `SettingsModal` and place it prominently in the main `RepoTxtFetcher` component, below the intro text and settings icon. The `SettingsModal` will now only contain the URL and Token inputs.

Here are the updated files:

**1. Mothership Component (`RepoTxtFetcher.tsx`)** - Modified

**2. Settings Modal (`/components/repo/SettingsModal.tsx`)** - Modified

**3. Other Subcomponents (No Changes Needed)**

*   `/components/repo/FileList.tsx`
*   `/components/repo/SelectedFilesPreview.tsx`
*   `/components/repo/RequestInput.tsx`
*   `/components/repo/ProgressBar.tsx`

These remain the same as in the previous refactoring step.

**Summary of Changes:**

1.  **Fetch Button:** Moved from `SettingsModal` to `RepoTxtFetcher`, placed centrally below the intro text/settings icon.
2.  **Settings Modal:** Now only contains URL and Token inputs. It receives the `loading` prop to disable inputs during the fetch process initiated by the main component.
3.  **Main Component (`RepoTxtFetcher`):**
    *   Includes the fetch button JSX and its associated logic (`handleFetch`, `extractLoading`).
    *   The settings toggle button now uses `FaCircleChevronUp` when the modal is open.
    *   Added a check in `handleFetch` to ensure `repoUrl` is not empty before starting.
    *   Updated the intro text slightly to guide the user.
    *   Updated status icons in the progress section to `FaCircleCheck` and `FaXmark`.

**Файлы в этом PR (6):**
- `components/repo/FileList.tsx`
- `components/repo/SelectedFilesPreview.tsx`
- `components/repo/RequestInput.tsx`
- `components/repo/ProgressBar.tsx`
- `components/RepoTxtFetcher.tsx`
- `components/repo/SettingsModal.tsx`

author: ericrisco
body:
This PR implements a simple but effective persistence layer using JSON files to store and retrieve vector database content.

## Persistence Implementation Details

- **Approach**: One JSON file per library, containing all related documents and chunks
- **Storage Structure**: Each library stored as a self-contained JSON with a clear hierarchical structure
- **Optimization**: Embeddings excluded from storage to minimize file size
- **Configuration**: Data directory configurable via `DATA_DIR` environment variable
- **Test Data**: Included Andorra dataset (`testing_data.json`) that can be loaded via `TESTING_DATA=true` flag

## Technical Considerations

- **Thread Safety**: Implemented fine-grained locking to prevent data races during file operations
- **Atomicity**: Library files written in a single operation to minimize corruption risk
- **Performance**: Optimized for read-heavy workloads with infrequent writes
- **Simplicity**: Straightforward implementation with no external database dependencies

## Intended Use Case

This persistence layer is designed for development, testing, and small to medium production deployments. The JSON approach offers excellent portability, readability, and ease of implementation while sacrificing some performance and scalability compared to dedicated database systems.

author: bberka
body:
## **v2.2**


### Features

- **Attachment Handling Overhaul:**
  - Implemented full support for attachment uploads to tickets. Attachments are now downloaded to the server and then uploaded to Discord.
  - The bot now reacts to mod messages containing attachments instead of deleting and resending the message, improving visual clarity.
  - Attachment URLs are now served from the application's domain instead of Discord's, providing better control and security.
- **Configurable Ticket Data Deletion:**
  - Added the ability to automatically delete ticket data (including attachments) after a configurable period. This feature can be enabled and configured in the options UI.
  - Introduced a daily job to handle the deletion process.
- **Optional Ticket Timeout:**
  - Ticket timeouts can now be disabled entirely. The default timeout value is now -1 (disabled). Existing tickets with a timeout value of -1 will not be automatically closed.
- **Configurable Statistics Calculation Period:**
  - Administrators can now configure the number of days used for calculating statistics. This setting is available in the options UI.
- **Public Attachment Access:**
  - Implemented a public API endpoint to serve attachment files based on their ID, enhancing accessibility.

### Bug Fixes

- **GuildOption Update Issue:** Resolved a bug where changes to `GuildOption` settings in the UI were affecting the cached reference without calling save changes. Caching has been disabled for the options page to ensure data consistency.
- **Invalid Ticket ID Handling:** The web UI now correctly redirects to a 404 page when attempting to view a transcript for an invalid ticket ID.
- **Blacklist Permission Check:** Fixed an issue where the `CheckUserBlacklistStatusQuery` incorrectly required user authorization.
- **Ticket Timeout Logic:** Modified the ticket timeout processing to only consider tickets with valid (non-disabled) timeout values.
- **Dependency Injection Issue:** Addressed a dependency injection issue with `AddHttpClient`.
- **Database Migration Issues:** Corrected database migration issues related to required fields and constraint minimum values.

### Improvements & Refactoring

- **Performance Optimizations:**
  - Optimized permission info retrieval by converting the result type to an array.
  - Improved performance by moving shared code to a common method and using `using` statements for variable scope management.
- **Codebase Cleanup:**
  - Removed an unused encryption key.
  - Removed the unused `MessageSent` color.
- **Queue Handling:** Migrated ticket attachment downloads to a singleton service for better management and dependency injection.
- **SmartEnum Naming:** Fixed the naming of the `HangfireQueueName` SmartEnum to comply with Hangfire's requirements (lowercase letters).
- **Query Simplification:** Inlined the `GetTimedOutTicketListQuery` into the job class, simplifying the codebase.

### Dependency Updates

- Updated NuGet packages to the latest versions.
- Added the `Microsoft.Extensions.Http` NuGet package for managing `HttpClient` instances.
- Added the `EntityFrameworkCore.Exceptions` NuGet package for better exceptions.
- Added the `EFCore.CheckConstraints` NuGet package for data validation.

body:
When specifying an option for a leapp CLI command using @add_option decorator, it has not been possible to specify a "falsy" value (or let's say empty) as `default` e.g. empty string, empty list, etc. Start to check NoneType for the `default` parameter properly to allow it to set this.

**Bump leapp-framework to 6.1.**

Note:
The similar problem is for `choices` and `metavar` parameters. In case of `metavar` it's however ok to ignore empty string. In case of empty `choices` it would lead to the same evaluation as in case of NoneType (any input is ok). So I that the `default` is the only parameter that needs to be checked properly.

author: cdelriot1121
body:
# **Optimización del Dockerfile para reducir tamaño y mejorar rendimiento**

### Descripción:
Este PR optimiza el Dockerfile dividiendo la construcción en dos etapas, lo que reduce el tamaño de la imagen y mejora el tiempo de ejecución.

### Cambios:
- **Etapa 1 (Compilación con Maven)**: Usamos una imagen `jdk` para compilar la app, descargamos las dependencias sin compilar, y luego construimos el `.jar`.
- **Etapa 2 (Imagen final)**: Usamos una imagen `jre` para ejecutar solo el `.jar`, eliminando dependencias de compilación innecesarias.
- **Reducción de tamaño**: Solo se incluye el archivo `.jar` y el JRE en la imagen final.
- **Exposición del puerto 8080** para acceder a la aplicación.

### Beneficios:
- **Menor tamaño de imagen** al separar la compilación de la ejecución.
- **Mejor rendimiento** en la construcción y ejecución de la imagen.

### Instrucciones:
1. Construir la imagen:
   ```bash
   docker build -t mi-app .
   ```
2. Ejecutar la app:
   ```bash
   docker run -p 8080:8080 mi-app
   ```

author: sozozzya
body:
This LLVM plugin performs an optimization that replaces expressions of the form `(a * b) + c (or c + (a * b))` with the intrinsic function `llvm.fmuladd(a, b, c)` in the Intermediate Representation (IR) of a program. This enables efficient use of the FMA (Fused Multiply-Add) instruction, which combines multiplication and addition into a single operation, potentially improving performance on architectures that support FMA.

1. **Traversal of Instructions in a Function:** The plugin traverses all functions in the module and looks for fadd (floating-point addition) instructions. For each such instruction, it checks if one of its operands is a multiplication (FMul).

2. **Replacement with llvm.fmuladd:** When an expression matching the pattern `(a * b) + c `or `c + (a * b)` is found, it is replaced with the call to the intrinsic function `llvm.fmuladd(a, b, c)`, which efficiently combines multiplication and addition in a single instruction.

3. **Removing Redundant Instructions:** After replacing the expression, the plugin removes the old fadd and fmul instructions, as they are no longer needed.

4. **Returning the Result:** If modifications were made, the plugin returns `llvm::PreservedAnalyses::none()`. If no changes were made, it returns `llvm::PreservedAnalyses::all()`.

body: This pull request updates the AKS module to resolve deployment errors by correctly configuring autoscaling for the PROD cluster. The changes remove unsupported nested autoscaling blocks, set node_count to null, and enable autoscaling by adding auto_scaling_enabled = true along with proper min_count and max_count values. Additionally, the network profile is updated with a custom service CIDR and DNS service IP to avoid conflicts with existing subnet CIDRs, ensuring that the TEST cluster maintains a fixed node count while the PROD cluster can scale dynamically between 1 and 3 nodes using AzureRM provider v4.25.0.

This pull request introduces a new logging feature to the `artio-relay` project, adding comprehensive logging capabilities for various events and requests. The changes span multiple files and include the creation of a new `Logger` class, integration of logging in the server and relay handling, and the addition of a new log model and adapter.

* [`pkg/logging/Logger.go`](diffhunk://#diff-825f311ea41486c0dfa097eac2eae4c7102e3fe155efb6bc6be41cafa216f18cR1-R68): Introduced a new `Logger` class with methods for logging different types of events (`LogConnect`, `LogDisconnect`, `LogPing`, `LogNIP11`, `LogRequest`, and `LogHandling`).
* [`pkg/relay/Relay.go`](diffhunk://#diff-011544029a283d0e8fe8685edc1fd0c29c0980ee4ba72b29a45c12f91a32bd1dR5): Integrated the new logging functionality into the relay handling process by adding calls to the `Logger` methods. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-540561ac49236a23922bb610eb8294ac6d6673f1bec93b1692dc5f9090a88ea1R5-R7) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-540561ac49236a23922bb610eb8294ac6d6673f1bec93b1692dc5f9090a88ea1R62-R63) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-540561ac49236a23922bb610eb8294ac6d6673f1bec93b1692dc5f9090a88ea1R104-L115) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-540561ac49236a23922bb610eb8294ac6d6673f1bec93b1692dc5f9090a88ea1L140-R135) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-540561ac49236a23922bb610eb8294ac6d6673f1bec93b1692dc5f9090a88ea1L163-R158) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-540561ac49236a23922bb610eb8294ac6d6673f1bec93b1692dc5f9090a88ea1R177-R182) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-540561ac49236a23922bb610eb8294ac6d6673f1bec93b1692dc5f9090a88ea1L220-R220) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-540561ac49236a23922bb610eb8294ac6d6673f1bec93b1692dc5f9090a88ea1L229-R229)

### Database Integration for Logs:

* [`pkg/storage/Storage.go`](diffhunk://#diff-c32846491109a0ac4a69f7baba922eca25ca40a371d8a1a404e676ff2a4df630L44-R44): Modified the `setupModel` function to include the new `Log` model in the database schema.

* [`pkg/storage/handlers/LogHandler.go`](diffhunk://#diff-0ed5a959b0a9df24b250e82af267fa675352f38a1f74a7f8e9bdb69a841a6036R1-R21): Added a new `LogHandler` class to manage the creation of log entries in the database.

### Additional Changes:

* [`pkg/relay/handlers/EventHandler.go`](diffhunk://#diff-a4ccbba5bc85012766a2b127b16abe26975dabf127059d5175687bb1be2973beL41-R59): Refactored the `Handle` method to use `WriteJSON` for error responses instead of returning formatted strings.

author: sufiyan-msa
body:
## Problem The `upper` template filter was incorrectly set with `is_safe=False` while the `lower` filter had `is_safe=True`. This inconsistency caused HTML-safe strings to be escaped when using the `upper` filter, which is not the expected behavior. ## Changes - Modified the `upper` template filter registration to set `is_safe=True` - This change makes the behavior consistent with the `lower` filter - Fixes the test case where HTML-safe strings should preserve their safety when using the `upper` filter ## Test Case ```python template = """ {{ html|upper }} {{ html|lower }} """ html = mark_safe("

Hello World!

") # Now correctly outputs: #

HELLO WORLD!

#

hello world!

``` ## Related Issue Fixes #36049 ## Bug Description The `upper` template filter was incorrectly set with `is_safe=False` while the `lower` filter had `is_safe=True`. This inconsistency caused HTML-safe strings to be escaped when using the `upper` filter. ## Impact When using the `upper` filter on HTML-safe strings (marked with `mark_safe`), the HTML tags were being escaped unnecessarily. For example: ```python html = mark_safe("

Hello World!

") # Before: <P>HELLO WORLD!</P> # After:

HELLO WORLD!

``` ## Solution Changed the `upper` filter registration to set `is_safe=True` to match the behavior of the `lower` filter. This ensures consistent handling of HTML-safe strings across both string case transformation filters. ## Testing Added test case to verify that HTML-safe strings maintain their safety when using the `upper` filter.

author: julianneswinoga
body:
Fixes #262 

- Updated CI to build with `INFO_DISPLAY_TYPE`, but only for `mksgenlv21` and `esp32`
  - Needed to add in some more constraints based on the firmware:
  - AVR-based boards can only have `DISPLAY_TYPE` OR `INFO_DISPLAY_TYPE`, not both
  - MKS Gen L-based boards can't have `INFO_DISPLAY_TYPE` and a focus motor (from their pin configuration)
- Fix the `https://github.com/ClutchplateDude/esp8266-oled-ssd1306#4.6.0` tag specifier, because the `4.6.0` tag is before @ClutchplateDude fixed the library. `4.6.2` tag is now correct.
- Apparently the `esp32` build with `INFO_DISPLAY_TYPE_I2C_SSD1306_128x64` was just broken? `pgm_read_byte()` on `esp32` (which is just a pointer cast because `esp32` doesn't actually have `PROGMEM`) does a useless cast which fails with our warning flags

* This is a fix to allow SocialPredict to work with newer versions of MacOS locally.
* (High Level Overview) There are known issues with Docker which deal with how Mac sets certain xattrs in files not allowing Docker to manipulate them directly on the disk, which means we need to mount our postgres volume.

author: markphamm
body:
# Pull Request: Add Route Cleaning Functionality

## Description
This PR adds functionality to clean and parse route information from flight reviews. The new functions break down route strings into structured components including origin city/airport, destination city/airport, and transit points (if any).

### Key Features
- Adds `parse_route` helper function to extract detailed route components
- Adds `cleaning_route_column` main function to process route data in DataFrame
- Handles various route formats including direct and connecting flights
- Extracts IATA airport codes and city names
- Preserves original route information while adding structured data

### Changes
- Added two new functions to `scripts/transform.py`:
  - `parse_route`: Helper function to parse individual route strings
  - `cleaning_route_column`: Main function to process route column in DataFrame
- Updated `main()` function to include route cleaning step
- Added route-related columns to output DataFrame

### Code Changes

```python
def parse_route(route: str) -> Dict[str, Union[str, None]]:
    """
    Parse a route string into origin, destination, and transit components,
    and further extract city and airport information.
    
    Args:
        route (str): The route string to parse (e.g., "London Heathrow to Paris CDG via Amsterdam")
        
    Returns:
        Dict: A dictionary containing the parsed components:
            - origin: The full origin string
            - destination: The full destination string
            - transit: The full transit string (if any)
            - origin_city: The extracted origin city
            - origin_airport: The extracted origin airport (3-letter IATA code)
            - destination_city: The extracted destination city
            - destination_airport: The extracted destination airport (3-letter IATA code)
            - transit_city: The extracted transit city (if any)
            - transit_airport: The extracted transit airport (3-letter IATA code)
    """
    # Map of airport codes to their cities
    AIRPORT_TO_CITY = cfg.AIRPORT_TO_CITY
    # Map of airport names/keywords to their 3-letter IATA codes
    AIRPORT_CODES = cfg.AIRPORT_CODES
    # Map of city names to their common airport codes
    CITY_TO_AIRPORT = cfg.CITY_TO_AIRPORT
    
    def extract_city_airport(location: str) -> Tuple[Optional[str], Optional[str]]:
        """
        Extract city and airport from a location string.
        
        Args:
            location (str): The location string to parse (e.g., "London Heathrow", "JFK", "Paris CDG")
            
        Returns:
            Tuple[str, str]: A tuple containing (city, airport) where airport is a 3-letter IATA code
                             and city is the proper city name (not the airport code)
        """
        if not location or pd.isna(location) or location.strip() == '':
            return None, None
        
        location = location.strip().lower()
        
        # Check for 3-letter codes that might be IATA codes
        iata_match = re.search(r'\b([a-z]{3})\b', location)
        if iata_match:
            code = iata_match.group(1).upper()
            # If it's a valid code in our dictionary
            if code in AIRPORT_TO_CITY:
                # Get the city for this airport code
                city = AIRPORT_TO_CITY[code]
                return city, code
            
            # If we don't know the city for this code but it's a valid format
            if code in [v for v in AIRPORT_CODES.values()]:
                # Try to extract the city from the location
                location_without_code = re.sub(r'\b' + iata_match.group(1) + r'\b', '', location).strip()
                if location_without_code:
                    return location_without_code.title(), code
                else:
                    # If we can't determine the city, use a placeholder
                    return "Unknown", code
        
        # Check for known airport names in the location
        for airport_name, airport_code in AIRPORT_CODES.items():
            if airport_name in location:
                # Get the city for this airport code
                if airport_code in AIRPORT_TO_CITY:
                    city = AIRPORT_TO_CITY[airport_code]
                    return city, airport_code
                
                # If we don't have a mapping for this airport code
                # Extract the city part from the location
                city_part = location.replace(airport_name, '').strip()
                if city_part:
                    return city_part.title(), airport_code
                else:
                    # If we can't determine the city, use a placeholder
                    return "Unknown", airport_code
        
        # Check for city names that have default airports
        for city_name, airport_code in CITY_TO_AIRPORT.items():
            if city_name in location and len(city_name) > 3:  # Exclude 3-letter airport codes
                return city_name.title(), airport_code
        
        # If we reach here, we couldn't identify an airport code
        # Return the location as the city and None for airport
        return location.title(), None
    
    if not route or pd.isna(route) or route.strip() == '':
        return {
            'origin': None, 'destination': None, 'transit': None,
            'origin_city': None, 'origin_airport': None,
            'destination_city': None, 'destination_airport': None,
            'transit_city': None, 'transit_airport': None
        }
    
    # Normalize the route string
    route = route.strip()
    
    # Initialize result dictionary
    result = {
        'origin': None, 'destination': None, 'transit': None,
        'origin_city': None, 'origin_airport': None,
        'destination_city': None, 'destination_airport': None,
        'transit_city': None, 'transit_airport': None
    }
    
    # Check if route contains 'via' for transit
    if ' via ' in route.lower():
        parts = route.lower().split(' via ')
        main_route = parts[0]
        transit = parts[1]
        
        # Split main route into origin and destination
        if ' to ' in main_route:
            origin_dest = main_route.split(' to ')
            origin = origin_dest[0].strip()
            destination = origin_dest[1].strip() if len(origin_dest) > 1 else None
        else:
            origin = main_route.strip()
            destination = None
        
        # Store the original values
        result['origin'] = origin.title() if origin else None
        result['destination'] = destination.title() if destination else None
        result['transit'] = transit.title() if transit else None
        
        # Extract city and airport for each component
        if origin:
            origin_city, origin_airport = extract_city_airport(origin)
            result['origin_city'] = origin_city
            result['origin_airport'] = origin_airport
        
        if destination:
            dest_city, dest_airport = extract_city_airport(destination)
            result['destination_city'] = dest_city
            result['destination_airport'] = dest_airport
        
        if transit:
            transit_city, transit_airport = extract_city_airport(transit)
            result['transit_city'] = transit_city
            result['transit_airport'] = transit_airport
    
    # For routes without transit
    elif ' to ' in route.lower():
        parts = route.lower().split(' to ')
        origin = parts[0].strip()
        destination = parts[1].strip() if len(parts) > 1 else None
        
        # Store the original values
        result['origin'] = origin.title() if origin else None
        result['destination'] = destination.title() if destination else None

author: pistonpercy
body:
I have been working on the autorouter on a private server for a while and was hoping to share my notes and hopefully merge some improvements.

# tl;dr

I made the autorouter work with 1862 and generally made some improvements to the router phase so it is more flexible to games with more complex routing + revenue rules.

- [Two](https://github.com/PistonPercy/18xx/commit/cf49e63d9ee0414ae31696a3d24b2d80af0b0daa) [patches](https://github.com/PistonPercy/18xx/commit/9b4ad8f6bb95043a2fc39b85dfc98e2bc6db3ad4) to fix pathing in 1862
- [A patch](https://github.com/PistonPercy/18xx/commit/aed4cff51507a5e82078c1633318c46c765311ef) to change routing to a simpler but more correct algorithm. It enables the autorouter to function for games that revenue can't be calculated per route independently and games that allow reusing tracks between different trains. 1862 is the easiest example of both. I expect this will require some refinement before being committed. I currently add a new button to choose which routing code to use, it's debatable if that's good for rollout (but was useful in early testing). I also think that having a `get_routing_rules` function on `Game` would be nice so we can avoid special casing titles in the autorouter and gives us a good place to expose this information in a declarative way (for what it is worth, as a user, I wish the game UI would expose the routing rules like they usually expose the market rules)
- [A fix](https://github.com/PistonPercy/18xx/commit/b56c2724cc8e5950a5ef05ff93641a61414d34aa) to the path generation because the new autorouter would generate routesets that the old autorouter never could.
- [A really bad](https://github.com/PistonPercy/18xx/commit/bc6e3774ec894f278cbff1eff3bf6aa142bc22d0) tool to test the autorouter using nodejs. A [less bad, but still wip](https://github.com/PistonPercy/18xx/commit/2ed823f3b5fb4cb90b57eed5d7d0cbbe5b228162) debugger for finding games where the game had paths that the pathing couldn't generate. Neither of these are mergable as is, but I'm sharing them to explore if a benchmarking/mass replay suite is useful. 


# Background on autorouter

The main parts of the autorouter are:
- pathing: finding all the valid routes for the trains
- routing: finding the combo of valid routes which are valid together that give the maximum value.

# Pathing

The primary source of bugs here are a mismatch of `check_other` expectations. As I understand `check_other` is only separate because the autorouter suppresses it in path generation. It is used to suppress rule checks for rules that require the full set of routes to validate.

As an example of rule that is suppose to be in `check_other`, in 1862, a route must visit the home token, but every path doesn't require visiting the home token. If that check isn't in check_other (which [it isn't](https://github.com/tobymao/18xx/blob/master/lib/engine/game/g_1862/game.rb#L1516)), we can only generate paths that visit the home token. Thus it is proper for the home token rule to be in `check_other`.

I'd also propose to rename `check_other` to `check_full_route_set` (or something better).

Other minor bugs:
- In 1860, a single train is able to go through a tokened out city, but the autorouter isn't able to generate routes going through tokened out cities because the [`blocks?`](https://github.com/tobymao/18xx/blob/68fd2453b54b00a1bc136fb9ba18470236f08931/lib/engine/part/city.rb#L37) will return true for tokened out city so the [graph walker](https://github.com/tobymao/18xx/blob/68fd2453b54b00a1bc136fb9ba18470236f08931/lib/engine/part/node.rb#L82) can't ever go through it

# Routing

## Current Algorithm

This is a bit of a high level view of the algorithm, but helps understand what it is doing.

1. Find all possible paths per train
2. Then call js_evaluate_combos which does
    1. Add the first train’s paths to a combo array
    2. For each train, for each route of that train
        1. for each combo in the combo array,
            1. js_route_bitfield_conflicts: Check if the route overlaps with the combo, if so continue the loop
            2. is_valid_combo: Check if the combo + route is a valid combo, if not, continue the loop
            3. Make newcombo with combo+route and calculate it’s revenue as combo.revenue + route.revenue
            4. Add newcombo to the new_combos array
            5. If newcombo revenue is more than the currently known most revenue, then add it to possibilities and set max_revenue
            6. If newcombo revenue is equal to the currently known most revenue, then add it to possibilities
        2. Set combo array to new_combos
3. Then we calculate the real revenue for each possibility and get return the possibility with the max revenue

## Problems/Bugs in Routing
- The combo and new_combo arrays scales with the number of valid paths and creates memory pressure and performance issues. I was actually getting out of memory issues in some testing.

- If `is_valid_combo` fails, then we toss out the combo even though adding a new train can make the combo valid in some variants (e.g. in 1862 adding a new train can make an invalid freight path valid)

- By using js_route_bitfield_conflicts, the auto router assumes routes must always use different tracks. This isn’t true in 1862 where different train can overlap on tracks.

- This algorithm assumes that a combo’s revenue is the sum of the routes revenues. This isn’t true in all variants (e.g. in 1862 where each city can only be counted once), so in these variants, the autorouter kind of returns a random variant. This can even kick in for games like 1846 (which has fairly basic rules) if you have the mail contract private company.

- The current autopather hangs the UI while pathing. This is frustrating for a variety of reasons, it means as users we can't just stop the router when it is "good enough" and the developer tools (like the profiler) are very difficult to use.

## Proposal To Fix Routing

I’d like propose to switch to a simpler, brute-force algorithm of checking all combinations of paths. I've been using this algorithm for a handful of games and it works pretty well.

The code is easily extended so that games can provide additional heuristics (mainly in "can this combinations of routes become the best set of routes if we add a train" and "estimate the upper bound of revenue of this set of routes"). I wish it wasn't worth doing this for some of the heavier maps/games, but the main problem is that calling ruby has some pretty severe performance traps (the main one I saw most often was returning from a lambda causes an exception to be thrown) and in general Opal seems to generate some expensive JS. It tends to be good enough in my experimentation without much customisation of the hooks, but I bet we could easily get an order of magnitude faster routing if we invested in better javascript only heuristics.

Some ideas of heuristic flags that games can provide:
- trains can't overlap (most games, but as an example 1862 can overlap tracks).
  This is actually implemented.
- trains must visit the home city (1860)
- [trains can visit a tokened out city once](http://www.fwtwr.com/18xx/rules_difference_list/7_2.htm)
- trains of different types can overlap (1822, 18 Los Angeles). This flag actually exists `TRAIN_AUTOROUTE_GROUPS`, but the new autorouter doesn't use it yet.
- train routes must intersect (1860)
- separating out single time per routeset revenue sources (E-W bonus + mail contract in 1846) so revenue estimate is more accurate

# Grab bag of other notes
- The autorouter being all in javascript embedded in ruby is rather difficult to work with.
- I found the fact that `Route` is mutable and depends on the route set that it is in extremely bug prone. It repeatedly bit me while working on these changes.

body:
Hi Lukas,

As previously discussed privately, this pull request introduces some optional improvements that align the action with a broader asset management focus.
With the introduction of the download ability, i've added a new `downloadPath` action input. To keep the inputs clear and consistent, I propose renaming the `zipPath` parameter to `uploadPath`.

These enhancements allow the action to handle both uploading and downloading of assets seamlessly, and they set the stage for evolving the tool into a comprehensive asset management solution rather than just an uploader.
It might also be worth considering a renaming of the action itself in the future to better reflect this expanded scope.

I'm open to your feedback.

Best regards,  
Nils

body:
## 🎯 Changes

Add an initial set of type benchmarks using `@ark/attest` with detailed explanations so they can be expanded and integrated with CI in the future.

By default, the bench threshold for a change is +20%, otherwise running the bench will return a non-zero exit code.

I was initially hoping to get some version of [this TypeScript PR](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/pull/61535) merged to address the sequential case demonstrated in `sequential.bench.ts`.

Since it may take a bit of additional time for the team to determine which solution they'd like to go with, I figured it was time to submit these now so tRPC can start benefiting from them.

Note, the data used to arrive at my broader conclusions can be found here:

https://github.com/ssalbdivad/trpc-tsperf

body:
#### PR Classification
This pull request introduces a restructuring of the data access layer, implementing a generic repository pattern and enhancing user management with ASP.NET Core Identity.

#### PR Summary
The changes enhance the project's architecture by implementing a generic repository and unit of work pattern, integrating soft delete functionality, and updating user management. 
- `IGenericRepository.cs` and `IUnitOfWork.cs` were added to define repository and transaction management interfaces.
- `GenericRepository.cs` and `UnitOfWork.cs` were implemented to provide concrete repository methods and transaction handling.
- `BankingSystemContext.cs` was updated to inherit from `IdentityDbContext<ApplicationUser>`, enabling ASP.NET Core Identity integration.
- Various configuration classes were modified to support soft delete functionality.
- Migration files were created or updated to reflect changes in the database schema, including new tables and relationships.

author: 7h3kk1d
body: # Configuration Mode * Adds a new configuration mode to Hazel for modifying some settings as Hazel programs * Includes 2 new configuration slides * Color theme configuration * Adds a dark mode * * Shortcut configuration * Allows for configuring of shortcuts bound to the ninja keys command palette * Adds a keybinding projector that listens to keypresses ## Issues (to be addressed in future prs) - There's a lot of duplication between configuration mode and scratchmode - The original version had them combined and I split them up. I think we want them to be able to diverge more and need a better story for the common parts between editors. - The configuration updates all happen through side effects - Otherwise it would require threading actions up/down the model stack - Duplication in config information - I just duplicated the color scheme from what's in the css files. - This should probably be addressed by having a yaml file with the defaults and having a build step to build the css and the segment. I would like to talk to @disconcision about having a more "intentional" colorscheme data type before investing in that though. - The shortcuts are just copied from the Shortcut.re file. We can't depend on it because of circular dependencies with Page.re. This seems solvable but requires some thinking about how to have a thread the types around. I think making ninjakeys context sensitive for actions should be done with this. - Eventually we should have stronger analyzed types for these editors and have a way to integrate with the default values

author: timacdonald
body:
We put things in the cache because the cache is fast; that doesn't mean hitting the cache is _free_.

This PR introduces a memoized cache driver. This new driver is a decorator around other cache drivers. It will remember values resolved from the cache and store them in memory for the remainder of the execution.

```php
Cache::get('foo');         // hits the cache
Cache::get('foo');         // hits the cache
Cache::get('foo');         // hits the cache

Cache::memo()->get('foo'); // hits the cache
Cache::memo()->get('foo'); // does not hit the cache
Cache::memo()->get('foo'); // does not hit the cache
```

The following illustrates the values returned:

```php
Cache::put('name', 'Taylor');
Cache::get('name');           // "Taylor"

Cache::put('name', 'Tim');
Cache::get('name');           // "Tim"

Cache::put('name', 'Taylor');
Cache::memo()->get('name');   // "Taylor"

Cache::put('name', 'Tim');
Cache::memo()->get('name');   // "Taylor"
```

The `memo` function accepts a driver name. This indicates the _real_ driver that the memo driver should decorate:

```php
// default driver...
Cache::memo()->get('name');

// redis driver...
Cache::memo('redis')->get('name');

// database driver...
Cache::memo('database')->get('name');
```

Each driver will get a unique memo decorator. This means values are not shared between different drivers:


```php
Cache::driver('redis')->put('name', 'Taylor in Redis');
Cache::driver('database')->put('name', 'Taylor in the database');

Cache::memo('redis')->get('name');    // "Taylor in Redis"
Cache::memo('database')->get('name'); // "Taylor in the database"
```

When you call a method on the memo driver that is intended to mutate the value in the cache, e.g., `put`, `remember`, etc., we forget the memoized value and then call the same method on the decorated driver:

```php
// assuming the default driver is 'redis'...

Cache::memo()->put('name', 'Taylor'); // writes to Redis
Cache::memo()->get('name');           // hits Redis
Cache::memo()->get('name');           // does not hit Redis
Cache::memo()->get('name');           // does not hit Redis

Cache::memo()->put('name', 'Taylor'); // forgets the memoized value for 'name' and writes to Redis
Cache::memo()->get('name');           // hits Redis
Cache::memo()->get('name');           // does not hit Redis
Cache::memo()->get('name');           // does not hit Redis
```

> [!NOTE]
> I had hopes and dreams that if you wrote to the cache via the memo driver we could actively remember the value. That way you don't need to retrieve it after a write. Unfortunately there were too many inconsistencies between drivers and different mutation methods for that to work. For example, when you call increment the value returned from the cache is an int. If you then retrieve that value via `get` it will be a string of the int.

The memo driver does not fire events. Events will be fired by the underlying driver if it is called.

When calling methods that mutate the cached value, the memo driver will always forget memoized value even if the call to the underlying driver fails.

One last bonus benefit of the memo driver is that is ensures consistent values from the cache throughout a request. Imagine you attempt to get the same key in two different places within a request and you get two different results because a different process updated the value or perhaps it _just_ TTLd out of the cache. That could cause unexpected runtime side effects on your application. Using `Cache::memo` ensures that you get the same result for the entire request or job lifecycle regardless of what happens in the cache while time progresses throughout the execution.

This idea has been bubbling away for a while and once we saw what was happening in some of our customers’ apps via Laravel Nightwatch, I knew we needed to make it happen.

author: universal-omega
body:
* Fixes numerous bugs with ManageWikiPermissions and ManageWikiNamespaces, including double logs, wrong logs, unformatted logs, missing permissions (like from a now-disabled extension) can now be removed. These were also not tracking changing probably so reloading could keep resubmitting the same form with no actual changes again and again creating numerous logs for it.
* Fixes numerous bugs with unformatted messages (like raw tags showing on page) in ManageWiki error messages and ManageWikiDefaultPermissions.
* Fixes a bug with OOUI caching that sometimes breaks switching between tabs (but there may be another cause also that may make it still happen as this one is hard to test)
* Fixes potential remote connections in ManageWiki permissions and namespaces.
* Fixes a bug where say there are 3 permissions on a group, you remove those 3 permissions but also add 1 more, the group still gets deleted because it only checked for removed permissions count === total permissions count, it now also checks if new permissions are being added before deleting it.
* Adds redirects back to the main ManageWiki module page when deleting groups and namespaces. This is to solve numerous bugs with change tracking if you reload multiple times when deleting groups and namespaces.
* Adds a filter-callback to make new groups created in ManageWiki lowercase. MediaWiki seems to treat them as lowercase anyway in UserRights for example so ManageWiki should also. Display names can be customized using interface messages.
* Caches credits on ManageWikiExtensions to improve performance.
* Renames `$wgManageWiki` to `$wgManageWikiModulesEnabled`
----
* Does full strict typing
* Adds ConfigNames
* Migrates to HookRegistry
* Migrates to JobSpecification
* Migrates to QueryBuilder
* Does a lot of service injection migration
---
* Removes RemoveSettings script since PopulateWikiSettings has a --remove option. This just fixes PopulateWikiSettings to work with --remove without requiring --sourcelist.

body:
Note that this (inherited) documentation layout is wonky, as it has the `javadoc` tree "inside" the Fusion module hierarchy, rather than as a sibling.  This is largely because we want to render this index from Markdown using the magic `fusion document` command, and that currently requires everything to be under `fusion/src` alongside module code.

We should eventually rework this so that the Fusion and Java references are sibling directories.
